author: ohtadmin
title: Narragansett Cafe to host open mic Wednesday
text:
The Narragansett Cafe will host its third open mic from 8-10 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 19.
The event, dubbed “Wednesday Night Live at the Ganny,” is free and open to the public on the third Wednesday of every month. People who want to perform can pre-register by e-mailing wedsliveganny@gmail.com; they also can register at the event.
Singers, instrumentalists, storytellers, standup comedians, poets and “anything else creative” are encouraged to perform. Each performer has the stage for 5-7 minutes.
Jane Gilgun, who produces the open mics, called them “community building” events that “taps into the loads of talent in Jamestown.” She read her poetry during the October edition.
“This was the best audience I ever had,” she said. “I couldn’t believe it. They were so welcoming. I read better than I ever had and was elated afterward. That has never happened before.”
Gilgun, emphasizing the “community” aspect of the event, said Nancy Beye, the president of the town council, baked a cake to celebrate one of the performer’s birthdays. Everyone got a slice.
Jay Primiano and Jan Greene, two writers and improv actors who also perform, are the emcees. Greene said the first event was standing room only.
“We are thrilled at the community’s response,” Greene said. “And it’s free. Many open mics have a cover charge.”
“The talented individuals from the first two open mics have made for some great entertainment,” added Primiano. “We have pros, near-pros and newcomers. ‘Wednesday Night Live at the Ganny’ has been more successful than I ever could have imagined.”
